title: Reranker regression playbook & labeler QA
content:
Summary:
This doc is a working playbook for building and auditing reranking evaluation sets used during model onboarding and regression detection. Focus: pairwise preference labels + NDCG calculations + slice analysis. Intended audience: label ops, applied ML engineers, and SREs running eval runs.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable labeling SOP for pairwise preference judgments.
- Define dataset slices that catch common regressions (novelty, tail queries, entity-rich queries, long contexts).
- Specify metric computations (NDCG@k, pairwise win-rate) and regression thresholds for alerts.
- Capture QA checks and inter-annotator agreement (IAA) procedures.

Dataset composition (target):
- 5k evaluation queries split across 8 slices (see below).
- For each query, collect: top-10 candidate ranking from baseline and candidate model, 10 pairwise comparisons sampled across rank positions.
- Pairwise pairs: prefer cross-model mixed pairs (one from baseline, one from candidate) plus within-model control pairs.
- Label budget: ~50k pairwise judgments / epoch for stable NDCG estimates.

Labeling protocol (annotator instructions):
- Task: For each pair (A vs B) return one of: A, B, tie, invalid.
- Preference rule (high-level): choose the response that is better for the user query in terms of relevance and correctness. Prefer concise, directly relevant answers; penalize hallucination, wrong facts, or omission of critical steps.
- Tie: use if both are equally good for user intent (not just similar wording).
- Invalid: use if the pair contains malformed text or is entirely irrelevant to the query (labeler should flag and skip).
- Examples (share in labeling UI):
  - Query: "How to rotate an image in PIL?"
    - A: code snippet that uses rotate(90) without import -> INVALID if missing context
    - B: code snippet with correct import and explanation -> B
  - Query: "Who wrote 'The Old Man and the Sea'?"
    - A: "Ernest Hemingway" -> A
    - B: "Hemmingway" (misspelling) -> A (prefer correct spelling if content matches)

Pairwise label schema (fields to capture for each judgment):
- query_id (string), pair_id (string), item_A_id (string), item_B_id (string), label (A|B|tie|invalid), annotator_id (string), time_ms (string), comments (optional).

Note: Because JSON schema for storage downstream expects flat fields, ensure labeling export includes these keys as strings.

Sampling strategy for pairwise comparisons:
- 40% cross-model top-k swaps (baseline top-5 vs candidate top-5), biased toward positions where models disagree.
- 30% within-model adjacent swaps (to measure consistency/noise).
- 20% long-tail queries upsampled (tail queries are <10-occurrence cluster).
- 10% safety/robustness probes (model instructions, instruction-following edge cases).

Metric computations (implementation notes):
- NDCG@k computation:
  - DCG@k = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i} - 1) / log2(i+1)
  - IDCG@k is DCG@k of ideal ranking (ordered by oracle relevance).
  - NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k
- Relevance mapping: convert pairwise labels to graded relevance per candidate by aggregating wins. One approach: for each candidate, rel = wins / comparisons -> then discretize into 0/1/2 bins by thresholds (0.0, 0.5, 0.8) for DCG input.
- Use bootstrapped confidence intervals (10k bootstrap samples across queries) to estimate NDCG variance.
- Report: NDCG@1, NDCG@3, NDCG@5 and mean pairwise win-rate vs baseline.

Regression detection thresholds (suggested):
- Alert if delta NDCG@3 <= -0.01 and p<0.05 (bootstrap).
- Secondary check: mean pairwise win-rate drops by >= 2 percentage points with p<0.05.
- Require at least one slice-triggered regression (see slices) before filing priority incident.

Slice definitions (operational):
- S1: Oracles (queries with curated gold relevance) — small set, high precision checks.
- S2: Tail queries (1-10 occurrences in sampled traffic) — often brittle.
- S3: Entity-heavy queries (3+ named entities) — tests entity linking and factuality.
- S4: Long-context (prompt length > 512 tokens) — tests KV cache/attention behavior.
- S5: Instruction-following (imperative intent) — tests instruction compliance.
- S6: Safety-sensitive (policy triggers or potentially harmful content) — must pass policy gate.
- S7: Numeric reasoning (contains numeric computation or logic).
- S8: UI snippets (HTML/JS/code examples) — tests formatting and code correctness.

Slice analysis plan:
- Compute NDCG@k per slice with bootstrapped CI.
- Compute delta relative to baseline per slice.
- Rank slices by effect size and by statistical significance.
- For significant regressions, attach 10 representative query examples with side-by-side outputs and labeler comments.

Labeler QA and IAA:
- Each pair labeled by 3 annotators (majority vote). Track Krippendorff's alpha or Fleiss' kappa; flag slices with kappa < 0.6 for relabeling/clarification.
- Weekly spot-check: PM/ML engineer reviews 50 random judgments and provides feedback to label ops.
- Annotator training doc: include 40 examples covering ties, invalids, and edge-case ambiguity.

Data hygiene checks (pre-run):
- No duplicate pair_ids across evaluation batch.
- Verify balance: at least 20% cross-model comparisons.
- Reject pairs where both candidates are identical or trivially different (stopwords).

Automation & analysis scripts (pseudocode snippets):
- Build relevance from pairwise wins:
  "for each query:
     for each candidate: rel_raw = wins(candidate)/total_comparisons(candidate)
     rel_bin = 2 if rel_raw >= 0.8 else 1 if rel_raw >= 0.5 else 0"
- NDCG computation: standard DCG/IDCG formulas above; use numpy/pandas for vectorized batch computations.

Alerting & triage runbook:
- If regression triggers: create Jira ticket (MLINF-REG-YYYYMMDD), tag model owners, attach slice report and 10 sample diffs.
- Triage steps: 1) reproduce locally on same dataset, 2) run qualitative review, 3) check rollout config (quantization, kernels), 4) rollback/pin to previous model if SLA-impacting.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm final discretization thresholds for relevance bins (Aisha to propose by 2024-12-08).
- Decide whether to weight human time by query frequency when aggregating NDCG across product (Marc).
- Evaluate alternate pairwise aggregation: Bradley-Terry model for continuous relevance scores (Sofia to prototype).

Action items:
- [ ] Finalize labeling UI prompts and examples (owner: Marc Chen).
- [ ] Add safety slice gating to labeling pool (owner: Sofia Ramirez).
- [ ] Implement bootstrap pipelines in rerank-eval repo (PR referenced above).
- [ ] Pilot 5k eval with new sampling strategy (Evan Brooks).

Notes (informal):
- Labelers consistently flagged long-context cases where model repeats previous dialogue — likely KV cache bug. Add these to S4 corner cases.
- Several annotators asked for a clear rule about punctuation differences — instructed to ignore trivial punctuation unless it changes meaning.

References & links:
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-eval/pull/87
- JIRA: MLINF-412 (eval infra improvements)
- Confluence: Onboarding-Reranker-Evals-Overview

End of doc.

(Notes-to-self: keep this doc short and link to the larger Confluence playbook once finalized; this is intentionally an operational checklist + labeling SOP to share with label ops.)
